blogs.content: Don’t Call It a Decision Model - TypeSafe AI Blog TypeSafe AI Enterprise Thoughts Company Docs API console Contact us API console Docs Menu ∵ Back Thoughts Thoughts Don’t Call It a Decision Model Nov 3, 2026 Nov 3, 2026 Nov 3, 2026 Jev makes judgments , code makes decisions . Allie Laabs, DevRel, TypeSafe We love that people have recognized the importance of the new category of models that Jev pioneered. It’s unsurprising that the term “decision models” has caught on as a name. When you first see Jev pick an option from a list, it’s easy to see it as making decisions. And indeed, we have used the word “decision” in our own education materials! So why is TypeSafe holding firm on calling Jev a System One model instead of a decision model? Let’s talk about it. The System One name comes from the concept Daniel Kahneman popularized in his book Thinking, Fast and Slow . System 1 thinking is fast and intuitive. System 2 is slower and more deliberate. With Jev, the emphasis is on fast, focused judgments, hence the System One name. It’s about where Jev fits in a system Let’s break down what a typical system is, using the metaphor of circuits: inputs on the left (your data, application state, etc), they flow into logic, and then outputs on the right. Let’s use a simplified version of the Customer Service workflow from our evals page as an example. The naive approach to using Jev in this workflow would be to place the entire decision in to a single Jev question: When people first see Jev, this is how they imagine it fitting in to systems: give it all of your state, and have it make a decision about what should happen . This often looks like one big Choice question, and stuffing lots of semantic descriptions of business logic and caveats in to the criteria field. While this can work, you will quickly find yourself engaging in what we call prompt gymnastics : tweaking these long explanations of conditions over and over to get each edge case handled. And then the next day you get some input you hadn’t thought of, the system fails, and you’re back to stuffing more caveats and clarifications in to criteria prose. What’s happening here is trying to put intelligence at the wrong layer of abstraction. Your system already knows the criteria for each of your expected outcomes, and only some of it actually requires judgement. The rest is cold, hard logic: When Exit reports an unauthorized charge Fraud team: freeze & dispute asks for a person, or threatens legal action Hand to a person wants money back, claim eligible, ≤ $25 Refund now wants money back, claim eligible, over $25 Refunds team reviews wants to cancel, subscription active, open to an offer Offer to stay otherwise Answer & continue So where does Jev fit in to this kind of system? To understand the answer, we need to peek inside to see what a decision is actually made of: Peel off the cap Decisions in a system are rarely one atomic choice. Peel off the cap and we find wires running from the inputs through nodes of code and nodes of judgment . Decisions in software, workflows, and business are built this way. Checking “claim eligible, unpaid” is math. Answering “does the user want money back?” takes judgment. That’s where Jev belongs, and it’s exactly what we mean by System One: the quick intuitive judgments a knowledgeable person makes in seconds. Code is great for answering what it can answer exactly. Jev answers only the small questions code can’t. Logic then combines those answers into the decision. It’s the combination of both judgement and code that allows a system to make reliable, observable decisions. Why Build It This Way 1. Clarity of design Reliable systems require a clear understanding of how decisions are made. By decomposing decisions into their atomic judgments and logic paths, we gain clarity about what actually flows through the system, and what edge cases need to be handled. 2. blogs.content: Company Harvey Adds Danish Legislation and its Preparatory Works Through Partnership with Djøf Forlag Content covering consolidated acts, the executive orders issued under them, and amendments and preparatory documents by Harvey Team • Nov 11, 2026 Today, Harvey announced a partnership with Djøf Forlag, one of Denmark’s most established legal publishers, to bring Danish legislation, executive orders and preparatory works into Harvey. Lawyers with a license to Djøf Forlag’s digital platform Jurabibliotek will be able to research and draft with the content alongside their own documents. The content covers consolidated acts, the executive orders issued under them, and amendments and preparatory documents. Lawyers can move between a provision, the regulations that implement it, and the material showing what the legislature intended, with each answer citing its source. The content can be used in Harvey Assistant, Agents, Vault, Workflows and Word Add-in, next to a team’s own notes, prior advice and matter documents. Example use cases include: Reading a provision against its intent: Checking what the preparatory works said when the provision was introduced. Moving from act to regulation: Following a statute to the executive orders that implement it. Advising from your own precedent: Drafting Danish-law advice from these sources and the firm’s own prior work. Jurabibliotek’s legislative content will be available in Harvey at the start of next year, with no additional charge. “Danish legal teams should be able to work with Danish law in the same place as the rest of their work. Djøf Forlag is one of the most established names in Danish legal publishing, and we’re pleased to bring its content into Harvey for the lawyers who rely on it,” said John Haddock, Chief Business Officer at Harvey. “The partnership brings Danish legislation directly to Harvey’s clients in Denmark. For more than 65 years, Djøf Forlag has provided Danish legal sources through books and, more recently, Danish legislation through Jurabibliotek. Increasingly, we see high demand from our customers to make those sources available in AI-powered legal tech systems, so partnering with Harvey is a natural next step,” said Bjarke Madsen, Digital Director at Djøf Forlag. “When we advise on a regulatory question, we start with the act, check the executive orders, and go back to the preparatory works when interpretation matters. With Djøf Jurabibliotek’s content in Harvey, we can do all of that alongside our own notes and prior advice, in the tool we already use to draft and review. That will make the work faster and more consistent,” said Christian Høyer Ørum, Executive AI Officer and Head of AI at Accura, which uses Harvey as its primary legal AI tool. Djøf Jurabibliotek’s licensed content sits alongside the Danish public sources already available in Harvey, and follows Harvey’s data partnership with Gyldendal Rettsdata in Norway. The partnership also builds on Harvey’s work with Danish firms including Accura and Kromann Reumert, leading Denmark-based law firms, which went live with Harvey across the firm earlier this year to scale research, drafting and review. blogs.content: Insights An MSA Review Should Test the Liability Cap Against Your Smallest, Riskiest SOW An MSA review sets the liability cap for SOWs you haven’t signed yet. See the three terms to test and how Harvey takes the first pass on an MSA. by Harvey Team • Nov 9, 2026 A master services agreement (MSA) sets the legal terms for a commercial relationship. Each statement of work (SOW) signed under it adds the scope, deliverables, and fees for one project. An MSA review is the legal review of those master terms before signature, and because SOWs usually inherit them, it also sets the rules for SOWs nobody has drafted yet. Take a hypothetical MSA your company is about to sign with an IT services provider. SOW-1 for implementation ($1.2 million) and SOW-3 for support ($300,000, billed annually in advance) are signed with the MSA. SOW-2, a $40,000 migration of customer personal data, follows four months later. All figures in this example are illustrative. Ten months after the MSA is signed, partway through SOW-2, a breach exposes the migrated customer data and leads to a $2 million claim against the provider. Whether the cap limits that claim to $40,000 or leaves room for all of it turns on a few words in the MSA's limitation of liability. Those words get settled during the MSA review, months before SOW-2 is written. We’ll follow this MSA from the provider’s first draft to the SOW-2 signature and show where legal AI helps. Harvey takes the first pass, finding the cap, precedence, and survival terms and comparing them with your playbook, so counsel’s time goes to the terms that decide the claim. The Cap Definition Decides Whether a $2 Million Claim Gets Limited to $40,000 The provider's draft caps its liability at the fees paid or payable under "the applicable SOW" in the 12 months before the claim. That reads as standard until you run it against SOW-2, the smallest SOW and the one carrying customer data. Here’s how far the same $2 million claim could go under three hypothetical cap wordings, assuming the cap is the only limit in play: Cap wording in the MSA (hypothetical) Cap Upper limit on the $2 million claim under this cap Fees under the applicable SOW (the provider's draft) $40,000 $40,000 Fees under all SOWs $1,540,000 $1,540,000 Fees under all SOWs, plus a data super-cap of the greater of $1 million or 3 times those fees $4,620,000 (3 times fees) for data protection claims $2,000,000, since the cap sits above the claim The provider’s draft lands at the bottom because the riskiest SOW carries the smallest fees. Counting fees under all SOWs, plus a data super-cap, puts the limit above the full claim. Harvey can do this reading for counsel. With the draft MSA, the SOWs signed alongside it, and the team’s executed MSAs in Vault, a review table lines up the cap wording against each SOW’s fees and against the cap positions the team has accepted before, each answer linked to its source. Counsel sees how small the cap gets on a low-fee, high-risk SOW before negotiation starts. A weak cap in the MSA carries into every SOW signed under it, which is why the cap sits near the top of any contract review checklist . An MSA Review Should Test Three Terms That Reach Into Future SOWs The cap basis, the order of precedence, and the termination and survival terms all bind SOWs that don't exist yet. Here's the hypothetical wording your team negotiated for each one, and why it matters for SOW-2. Harvey checks each of these terms in the provider’s draft against your playbook and marks where the draft departs from it, so counsel negotiates three clauses instead of hunting for them in a long draft. Which experiences in government most shaped how you think about the pressures on the public sector for those working in law, or law adjacent areas? Government and public agencies face many challenges. Cases collapsing because of incorrect disclosure. Decisions in immigration cases being judicially reviewed because a step in the process had been missed. And significant backlogs in our courts. I saw first-hand how the pressures on government were growing: the explosion of evidence in criminal cases, the rise in cases coming through our courts, and an overstretched prison system. In government, we were looking to technology to bring new answers to old problems. In the NHS, for example, da Vinci robotic-assisted surgery was helping patients with prostate cancer, and predictive analysis was being used to bring down waiting lists. It was obvious to me that technology could fundamentally change every area of government, including the justice system. What did you see in Legora that persuaded you to take on a bigger role with the company ? Three things matter to me: I want to work for a company that is bringing about positive societal benefits through AI. I want a can-do, positive culture, with dynamic leadership driving that change. And I want a company that truly works in partnership with its clients, listening to their needs and building its products on feedback and collaboration. I see all of this at Legora. Its tools can fundamentally change the delivery of legal and legal-adjacent public services. Tools for legal research and factual analysis save significant time and cost, and more broadly they can bring order to disorder in the management of legal processes. Its operating model relies on legal engineers, lawyers who work alongside the technical teams, so there is a real culture of collaboration with clients. Under Max’s incredible leadership, Legora has come further, faster, than any company in legal technology. In a very short time, it has built a brand that law firms recognise and trust. We want that same collaborative model to extend into the public sector, working in partnership with government to solve the problems it faces in delivering better, more streamlined services to citizens. What are the biggest obstacles to modernising the justice system with technology, and what would give decision makers the confidence to move faster? Many of our departments have legacy IT systems and those that work within government are understandably concerned about change and how to implement that change. We need to remind ourselves that not embracing technology also brings significant risk. What gives decision makers confidence is seeing it work for themselves. I would recommend that any public body tries a supplier before it buys. Legora included. For the public sector, we say that trust is not a differentiator; it’s a precondition. blogs.content: Insights Find Every Auto Renewal Clause in Your Portfolio Before its Notice Window Closes An auto renewal clause can set a notice deadline months early. Sort contracts by renewal mechanism, map 30 to 180-day windows, and give each one an owner. by Harvey Team • Nov 6, 2026 An auto renewal clause, also called an automatic renewal clause, extends a contract for another term unless a party gives notice by a set deadline. Tracking that deadline on one agreement is simple. A portfolio multiplies the deadlines, and Zylo's 2026 SaaS Management Index found that the average organization manages 211 SaaS renewals annually, before IT services and facilities agreements are counted. Take a hypothetical in-house team with about 400 supplier agreements across SaaS, IT services, and facilities. In this example, 260 of them renew automatically on January 1 unless someone gives notice. Their notice periods run 30, 60, 90, or 180 days, so the deadlines fall anywhere from July 4 to December 1. Reading 400 agreements for the same few renewal facts is the slow part, and AI can take it on. Harvey's review tables pull each agreement's renewal terms into columns linked to the source clause, so the team's time goes to checking those facts and deciding what to renew. We'll follow this team from sorting its contracts to getting each owner's decision in before the notice deadline. An Auto Renewal Clause Extends the Term Unless Someone Gives Notice in Time An automatic renewal clause sets four facts to capture: the renewal term, the notice period, who can give notice, and how notice must be delivered. Here's a sample clause from one of the team's agreements, a $240,000-a-year analytics subscription, written for this example: "This Agreement will renew automatically for successive twelve (12) month renewal terms. Either party may prevent renewal by giving the other written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term. All notices must be delivered to the addresses set out in Section 14.2." Read as data, it gives a 12-month renewal term, a 60-day notice period, a right either party holds, and a delivery rule that points to Section 14.2. A contract auto renewal clause often splits those facts across sections, so the notice address may sit in a general notices clause or in a later amendment. Missing any one of them can leave a notice of non-renewal open to challenge. The Renewal Mechanism Decides Whether Silence Keeps a Contract or Ends it Before any date matters, each contract needs a label for what happens if nobody acts. An auto renewal contract keeps running on silence, while an option to renew lapses on silence, so the two call for opposite actions. Here's how the team's 400 agreements sort, with all counts hypothetical: Renewal mechanism What happens if nobody acts Who has to act, and by when Agreements in this example Automatic renewal for a fixed term The contract renews for the stated renewal term The party that wants out, by giving notice of non-renewal before the notice deadline 300, including the 260 that renew on January 1 Evergreen, terminable on notice The contract keeps running, often month to month, until someone ends it The party that wants out, by giving notice that takes effect after the notice period 45 Option to renew The contract expires at the end of its term The party holding the option, by exercising it before its deadline 25 Fixed expiry The contract ends on its stated date Both parties, by signing a new agreement or an extension before that date 30 Some lawyers use "evergreen clause" for any automatic renewal, and others reserve it for contracts with no fixed renewal term, as the table does. Whichever label your team uses, record what silence does, since that decides whether a contract has a deadline to watch. The rest of this example follows the 260 January 1 renewals. blogs.content: Product Introducing Harvey’s Fact Graph for Disputes, Litigation, and Investigations The Harvey fact graph helps disputes, litigation, and investigations teams find and connect facts across millions of documents and build on one evolving record. by Harvey Team • Nov 5, 2026 We’re introducing Harvey’s fact graph, a new capability for disputes, litigation, and investigations teams to find and connect facts across millions of documents. It links those facts to supporting sources, to one another, and to the people, events, and issues they concern—helping teams uncover relationships across the full record over the lifetime of a matter. The fact graph is the newest addition to Harvey Graph , the connected map of legal knowledge and matter context that Harvey’s agents draw on to find the right information, cite it, and carry it forward. From Individual Facts to a Strategic Narrative In litigation and investigation matters, the job is to connect thousands of facts into a strategic narrative: who knew what and when, whether accounts hold up against the evidence, and where the record has gaps. The facts of a matter often seem disconnected, and the work requires ongoing resources to comb through huge volumes of information. An email might show that an executive received a warning about a defect. Meeting notes months later might record their approval of a product launch despite knowledge of the defect. Extracting and connecting those facts helps teams trace actions, assess what the evidence supports, and identify what still needs to be established. blogs.content: Insights AI Fluency in Legal Hiring and How to Show it “Comfortable with AI tools” in a job description tells candidates very little. Instead, firms can offer a common scale for AI fluency that shows students and junior lawyers what firms expect, and gives them a way to prove themselves fluent. by Peter Duffy • Nov 5, 2026 AI fluency is fast becoming a hiring priority for law firms. It means knowing how to use AI effectively in legal work, recognize its limitations, and apply your own judgment to its outputs. For students thinking about recruitment, that raises a practical question: What exactly do firms want students to know regarding AI, and how do you show you’ve got it? A few firms are leading the way with clarity around expectations. One recruitment post I came across recently opened with a single question: “Are you a lawyer who builds?” The post didn't come from a legal tech start-up or an alternative legal service provider, but a newly launched AI-forward practice set up by a leading European law firm. To explain what it meant, the firm pointed candidates to Levels 4 and 5 of Harvey’s recently published AI Fluency Framework : Builders , who create reusable AI tools such as agents and playbooks, and Catalysts , who build for others and set the standards around them. From AI Familiarity to Clear Expectations A few years ago, it would have been unusual to see law firms recruit explicitly for Builders and Catalysts. In the case of the aforementioned recruitment post, the firm made it clear that it needs lawyers who create with AI, not just use it, and it used the framework's levels to outline their expectations. This example shows how the ideal candidate profile has changed and what law firms are looking for specifically — not just an introduction to AI but the ability to build agents and think critically about how and when to use AI, pointing to a clear framework to attain and measure those skills If firms and candidates share a common language for AI fluency, the framework works just as well at the hiring stage as it does for a junior lawyer in development inside the firm. A firm built around AI is likely to be a step ahead of the wider market, but its hiring expectations are an early sign of where recruiting is heading, and quickly. Among the most progressive firms, AI fluency is already a skill set in rising demand. Expectations are getting clearer — and higher. For students, that makes it worth understanding those expectations now, before they become the norm. The Problem With "Comfortable With AI Tools" Look beyond the most AI-forward employers, and the picture is less precise. Many legal job descriptions mention AI in some form: "comfortable with AI tools," "tech-savvy," "keen interest in legal innovation." These phrases signal a firm's intent, but they set a tone without setting a bar. Comfortable doing what? Using AI to summarize a contract, identify key obligations, and check the summary against the source? Using AI to analyze deposition transcripts, identify inconsistencies, and verify findings against the record? Building an agent that teammates or a practice area can rely on, with clear instructions and review steps? Spotting where AI could reshape how a whole team works, then guiding changes to workflows and working practices? These are very different levels of fluency. Today every role can benefit from a clear standard, and for most lawyers that standard should be Proficient : regular, confident use of AI on substantive legal work. Where firms need Builders or Catalysts, being specific matters even more. The same clarity helps throughout a lawyer's career. A shared standard gives interviewers a consistent way to assess AI capability, gives development plans a clear destination, and shows both current and future lawyers what their goals should be, how to develop, and what their next step looks like. Approval matrices often key sign-off to contract value, type, or department. Those gates still decide who approves the deal and who signs, but they say little about who should decide a term that moved away from your standard position. Take a hypothetical customer master services agreement (MSA) worth $400,000 a year, which Sales submits on a Thursday on the customer's paper. The customer asks for a liability cap of 24 months' fees and uncapped indemnity for data breaches. It also wants the right to assign to an acquirer and the right to give notice of non-renewal 60 days before the term ends. Following that MSA from intake to signature shows who approves which term, with what evidence, and on which version. Value Thresholds Decide Who Signs, and Changed Terms Decide Who Approves Them Contract value, contract type, and the contracting entity remain the right triggers for financial and signature gates. A $400,000-a-year deal may need finance approval and a signatory with matching authority even when every term is standard. Those triggers can't tell you who should decide a cap the customer rewrote, so the matrix needs a second dimension keyed to deviations from your playbook. Here's how the MSA's four requests map onto that second dimension: Request in the MSA Status against your playbook Who decides What the decision-maker needs Notice of non-renewal 60 days before the term ends Matches the fallback, since your standard is 90 days and your fallback accepts 60 Contract manager, within delegated authority The fallback rule the request matches Assignment to an acquirer, with no notice Conditional, because the fallback allows it only with written notice Contract manager proposes notice language, and counsel decides if the customer refuses it The fallback, the proposed language, and the customer's response A cap of 24 months' fees Outside the fallback, which stops at 18 months Commercial counsel, within the exception authority your policy gives legal The customer's exact language, your standard and fallback, and prior deals with similar requests Uncapped indemnity for data breaches Shifts risk the business has to own Counsel advises, privacy and insurance stakeholders weigh in, and the CFO, as risk owner for this deal, accepts or rejects the risk The exposure in plain terms, insurance limits, and alternatives such as a separate cap for data-breach claims Two of the four requests can move in a delegated lane once they meet every condition of the fallback, so counsel's exception time goes to the cap and the indemnity. That lane depends on fallbacks legal has written down and formally delegated. Some triggers add a reviewer whatever the deal size, including personal or regulated data, IP ownership, an unfamiliar governing law, insurance requirements, or an unusual contracting entity. Sixty percent of contracts had drafting errors. When a self-driving car crashes, it makes the news. The scrutiny is warranted, but the headlines obscure the baseline. Human drivers cause far more crashes . They happen every day, yet almost none become media stories. In legal work, AI hallucinations also get the headlines. An AI-generated legal brief citing non-existent case studies. A judge who used AI to create a restraining order and misquoted state law. These are real issues that deserve attention. But Spellbook sees a different side to AI’s impact on legal and contract workflow. We see the human mistakes that are made when volume and complexity are met with limited hours and manual review. In fact, our data shows saved hours, greater accuracy and increased output when AI is deployed. So we decided to dig into the data to prove what we already know intuitively—humans make mistakes too. Using Spellbook Reviews, we analyzed 3,000+ SEC-filed contracts from over 500 companies, spanning 22 years. These were executed agreements from some of the largest and most heavily lawyered companies in the world. The findings showed plenty of interesting trends and fun examples. Six in ten contracts contained drafting issues. Many were minor. But one in 40 was high-risk—defined as changing the meaning of an agreement in a substantially negative way for at least one party—and they were concentrated in provisions that decide who gets paid, who carries the liability, and what happens in a dispute. None of this is a matter of carelessness by lawyers so much as a consequence of the length, complexity, and disjointed nature of how these types of SEC-filed agreements are prepared and negotiated. In this context, mistakes are inevitable. But they don’t have to be. Every company, public or private, will eventually run its contracts through products like Spellbook that will not only spot errors and risks immediately but suggest fixes based on a company’s own agreement context and real-time market data. Issue Example: A loan cap written two different ways. A mining company's loan agreement set its borrowing limit at "One Million Five-Hundred Sixty Thousand Dollars," then printed the figure beside it as $1,750,000.00. The words and the number differ by $190,000, and the mismatch appears twice. If the borrower and lender ever disagree, the contract gives a court no clear answer, and $190,000 turns on who wins. Findings at a Glance This study should be treated as a proxy for how much humans miss. We kept our analysis deliberately narrow, counting only objective drafting mistakes we could verify from the document itself. We could not judge whether an agreement was signed out of policy, drifted off market, or if a company gave away more than it should, let alone what sits inside the millions of private contracts. These numbers should be thought of as the floor, not a full account of everything worth fixing in an agreement. blogs.content: Insights When a Business Reorganizes, Each Assignment Clause Decides Which Contracts Move An assignment clause decides which contracts move freely when a business reorganizes. See a sample clause, consent and merger rules, and a review table. by Harvey Team • Nov 3, 2026 An assignment clause says whether a party can transfer its rights or obligations under a contract to someone else, and on what terms. A restrictive version, often called an anti-assignment clause, requires the other party's consent or limits transfers to named exceptions. A change of control clause can extend that restriction to a sale of the party itself. When a business reorganizes, sells a unit, or raises money, those clauses decide which contracts go with the business. Take a hypothetical software company, OpCo, that's moving its payroll analytics product line into a new wholly owned subsidiary, NewCo. The move covers 240 contracts, including customer agreements, supplier contracts, inbound software licenses, and an office lease in San Jose. About a year later, an outside investor plans to buy 30% of NewCo, and a lender plans to extend a credit line secured by NewCo's receivables. Every company, contract count, and clause in this example is hypothetical. OpCo will transfer the contracts directly, so the reorganization is an assignment of contract rights and duties from OpCo to NewCo. The 240 contracts mix services, sales of goods, software licenses, and a lease, and each type follows its own rules. Results turn on each clause's wording and governing law, so counsel confirms each conclusion for the states involved. Sorting 240 contracts by hand means reading the same few clause types again and again. AI changes that step. Harvey's review tables, for example, pull each contract's assignment terms into columns counsel can check against the source, so lawyer time goes to the consents and judgment calls. A Sample Assignment Clause Shows the Six Phrases That Decide a Transfer OpCo's customer form, used in 160 of the 240 contracts, has a contract assignment clause like this hypothetical one, with its six key phrases numbered: "Neither party may assign this Agreement (1) , whether voluntarily, by operation of law (2) , or otherwise, without the other party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld (3) . Either party may assign this Agreement to an Affiliate, or to a successor to the business it relates to, on written notice and without consent (4) . A Change of Control of a party is deemed an assignment (5) . Any attempted assignment in breach of this Section is void (6) ." The table reads each numbered phrase against OpCo's move: Phrase What it can do What it means for OpCo (1) "Assign this Agreement" Reach rights, duties, or both, depending on how the governing law reads it The move delegates OpCo's duties, so the ban reaches it under either reading (2) "By operation of law" Pull a merger into the restriction, depending on the deal structure and the state Doesn't decide a direct transfer, but would matter if NewCo later merged (3) "Shall not be unreasonably withheld" Generally require a reasonable basis to refuse consent outside the carve-outs Matters only if NewCo falls outside the Affiliate carve-out (4) "To an Affiliate... on written notice" Move the contract without consent, if the assignee meets the defined term and notice follows the notice section Decides the reorganization for the 160 contracts on OpCo's form (5) "Change of Control... deemed an assignment" Treat an ownership change as a transfer, measured by the defined term Decides whether the later investment in NewCo counts (6) "Void" In some states, make a noncompliant transfer ineffective instead of a breach that leaves a damages claim Raises the cost of a missed notice or consent The other 80 contracts use different assignment language, so the rules behind each phrase matter. See how deal context sets counsel's order, how clauses interact, and what to read before signing. by Harvey Team • Nov 2, 2026 A contract risk assessment finds the terms in an agreement that could cost your organization money, data, or control, and decides what to do about each one. Contract risk analysis checklists and likelihood-and-impact matrices tell you which kinds of risk to look for. Under a deadline, counsel also has to decide which provisions in this contract, for this deal, get a second look first. Take a hypothetical request that lands at 3:00 p.m. on a Friday afternoon. The VP of Support wants the contract for an AI customer support platform signed by Monday, at $180,000 a year, billed annually in advance. The provider's paper comes in three parts: a master services agreement (MSA), an order form, and online terms the MSA pulls in by URL. The platform will read your support tickets, so it will hold your customers' names, email addresses, and order histories. We'll follow this request from Friday afternoon to Monday's signature. Harvey reviews all three documents first, and counsel uses those results to rank the provisions that need a second look and to check the final copy before signing. Harvey's First Pass Turns Three Documents Into Four Flags Against Your Playbook The three documents go through Contract Intelligence, Harvey's contract review AI . It checks each document against your team's standard positions, which Harvey can build from contracts you've already signed.Those positions live in your contract playbook , and clauses that no rule covers get flagged as well. In this example, four provisions come back flagged. The provider's right to train its models on customer data, its right to add subprocessors by updating a web page, and a 36-month auto-renewal each depart from your positions. The MSA's change-in-terms provision matches no rule at all, so it goes to counsel for manual review. It lets the provider update its online terms by posting them, and it makes those terms control in a conflict. Your playbook in this example accepts a 12-month cap for software subscriptions, so the provider's cap doesn't come back as a deviation. Counsel also checks precedent. In this example, two earlier AI tool agreements that process customer data closed with a separate, higher cap for data-protection breaches. In Practice: At Repsol , review of a single contractual clause used to take the compliance team 30 to 60 minutes. With Harvey, the team has cut that time by over 90%, typically to a few minutes. This In Practice episode shows how legal teams build and run Playbooks directly in Word, the kind of review the support platform's paper gets on Friday. blogs.content: Insights What the Data Shows About Legal AI Adoption Harvey usage data shows how legal AI adoption is growing across seniority levels, practice areas, and markets, offering lessons for firms planning a rollout. by Katie Burke and John Haddock • Oct 30, 2026 Two years ago, the question most law firms asked about AI was whether to adopt it. Today, the questions we get surround how much, how fast, and at which levels organizations are adopting AI, so we thought it might be helpful to ground the discussion in data from our hundreds of thousands of users. Partners Represent Nearly a Quarter of Harvey’s Law Firm Users Let’s start with the most common misconception we hear about AI and legal, which is the trope that “only junior associates use AI.” The number of Harvey users who are partners is more than 4x what it was this time last year. Partners now represent 23% of Harvey’s law firm users, nearly a quarter. This is significant for a few reasons: not only are partners regularly using and seeing value with AI, but they are also helping set the tone for their organizations on responsible adoption of AI in their daily work. In addition to being clear from the data, we see this regularly in our customer feedback and discussions with law firms. At this year’s US Open, a very AI-savvy partner made the rounds to ask about the best agent their team was using regularly. This is not an accident — partners have moved from encouraging their associates to use AI and being open to experimentation and shifted into more daily usage and adoption by the senior partners within firms. The Tone on AI Starts at the Top The incentive for partners to use AI is not just their own work product and daily habits. When partners are more engaged, associates are notably more likely to use AI more frequently. Associate utilization rates were 25 points higher when Partner utilization was in the top quartile, which is one of the many reasons we highly encourage partners to join our adoption workshops and training in rollout planning. We met with a law firm that was considering Harvey who asked if it was okay if a few of the partners who participated in the pilot could share examples and use cases as part of the firm-wide rollout of Harvey. Not only is that welcome, it’s encouraged — there is no one who understands your organization better than the folks who work in it daily, so our approach to training and transformation is always to work deeply to earn and maintain the trust of your partners and your team. blogs.content: Insights Turning a Raw Deposition Transcript Into a Usable Record Learn how litigation teams turn deposition transcripts into source-linked, usable records for case strategy, drafting, and trial preparation. by Harvey Team • Oct 29, 2026 By the time a deposition ends, a litigation team may have hundreds of pages of testimony and very little time to turn it into something useful. The transcript preserves what was said, but it doesn’t tell you which admissions matter, where a witness’s account shifted, which exhibits carry the point, or how the testimony fits with the rest of the record. An AI deposition summary can shorten that first pass. What’s more valuable is a working record organized around the issues in dispute, linked back to the underlying testimony, checked against the operative transcript, and structured for whatever the team needs to do next. A Deposition Transcript is the Record, but Not a Working Case Tool Depositions are organized in the order that questions were asked, not necessarily in the order a lawyer will later need the facts. Witnesses might discuss the same issue at several points, qualify an answer thirty pages later, or refer to an exhibit that only becomes important once another witness is deposed. A usable record reorganizes that testimony around the case. It should make it easy to see what the witness admitted or denied, where the account changed, what events belong on the chronology, which documents matter, and where the team needs to follow up. This way, the transcript remains the source of truth, while the working record makes it more efficient to use. Before Summarizing, Confirm Which Version of the Transcript You’re Working From Transcript analysis gets harder to trust when the team isn’t clear on which version sits underneath it. Before you summarize, extract, or compare testimony, identify whether you’re working from a rough transcript, a final transcript, or a version that’s been corrected. Distinguish a Rough Transcript From the Final Certified Record A rough transcript can be useful when the team needs to start analysis immediately after the deposition. Treat that work as provisional, though. Wording, formatting, and page-line references may change before the final certified transcript is available, so check quotations and pinpoint references again before using them in a filing, examination outline, or other work product. Incorporate Corrections and the Errata Sheet If the witness later makes permitted changes, those updates need to travel with the analysis. In federal practice, Rule 30(e) provides a process for reviewing the transcript or recording and listing changes and the reasons for them when review was requested before the deposition ended. Other jurisdictions may handle the process differently, but the practical point is the same. A summary created before an errata sheet or other correction is incorporated may no longer reflect the operative record. Preserve the Source Structure From the Beginning Keep the reference information that helps a lawyer get back to the testimony quickly. This typically includes page and line numbers, speaker, exhibit references, and any other useful transcript markers. Stripping those details out may make a summary look cleaner, but it also makes every important finding harder to verify and cite later. Choose the Deposition Summary Format Based on What the Team Needs to do Next No single deposition summary format works for every task. The right structure depends on the job the summary needs to support, and the same transcript may justify more than one output. Page-Line Summaries Make Precise Testimony Easier to Retrieve Use a page-line summary when the team expects to return to exact testimony often. These work especially well for impeachment preparation, motion drafting, witness outlines, and any task where the reader needs a concise description of the answer next to a clear and precise source reference. blogs.content: Insights Extending Legal Agent Bench to U.S. Case Law Introducing a new extension to Legal Agent Bench that tests frontier models’ ability to research and draft litigation briefs end-to-end using real case records. by Laura Toulme and Julio Pereyra • Oct 29, 2026 Today we introduce LAB: United States Case Law (LAB: USCL), an evaluation framework for testing frontier models’ ability to research and draft litigation briefs end-to-end using real case records. LAB: USCL adds novel approaches to LAB for understanding model behavior by building environments from real, public data collected by Free Law Project and evaluating model-written briefs head-to-head. We find that a small group of frontier models can now research and write complete, first-draft briefs in a single shot with no attorney guidance. While these briefs still exhibit a long tail of failure modes, they are substantially closer to the high bar for filing with a court and mark a substantial advance on a task that demands complex legal reasoning and advocacy. In this post we discuss our initial findings on these emerging capabilities as well as how we plan to make research in this area more accessible in partnership with Grubel. Brief Writing: An Ultra-Long Horizon Task When parties to a litigation want a court to act, they file a motion: a formal request asking the judge to issue a specific order or ruling. A motion may ask the court to do routine things like change a deadline or take more dramatic actions like dismissing a case or sanctioning a party. Some motions are opposed by the other parties, who argue that it would be legally incorrect or otherwise inappropriate for the court to take the requested action. To support these more contested motions, parties file briefs: written advocacy explaining why the court is justified in taking some action based on the state of the case, the law and precedent, and other considerations. Brief writing is one of the most complex tasks in litigation, sometimes requiring a team of lawyers multiple weeks to write and refine a compelling argument. An agent replicating this work must complete the same three steps a lawyer does: understanding the state of the case, researching the case law, and writing the brief itself. Understanding the State of the Case. For agents, the first part of replicating this work is understanding the state of the case by reviewing its docket, the official record of the case’s proceedings. The docket lists every filing, meaning every document submitted to the court, such as the complaint that starts the lawsuit, the motions and briefs that contain the parties’ arguments, and exhibits supporting those arguments, such as contracts, letters, or financial records. It also records the judge’s orders and rulings. In complex or long-running cases, the docket can span thousands of filings. Figure 1. A sample PACER docket with identifying details anonymized. A docket lists filings and court actions in chronological order, with hyperlinks to download the underlying documents. Researching Case Law. The next step is case law research: finding the past court decisions that bear on the legal questions in a case and determining how much weight each one carries. When judges rule on motions or decide cases, they often explain their reasoning in written opinions. Together, these opinions make up case law, the body of rules that comes from judges’ decisions, as opposed to rules passed by legislatures (statutes) or issued by agencies (regulations). These decisions carry weight because they create precedent. In the United States legal system, judges are expected to justify their decisions by relying on earlier opinions. Some of those opinions are binding: a court must follow decisions on the same legal question from higher courts in its jurisdiction. blogs.content: Week 32 · August 3–7, 2026 Copy page Copy page Claude Code sessions message each other, self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your infrastructure, and auto mode becomes the default permission mode. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.220 → v2.1.224 3 features · August 3–7 Cross-session messaging v2.1.224 Your Claude Code sessions can now message each other. Claude discovers your other sessions with the ListAgents tool and sends with SendMessage , either when you ask it to or on its own, such as after a change in one session affects what another is working on. A message is text Claude writes for the other session, never your conversation history or files. Available on macOS and Linux. Requires v2.1.224 or later. With two sessions open on the same machine, ask one of them to pass something along: Claude Code Tell the session working on the payments API that users.name is now users.display_name The other session shows a Message from row once Claude has read the message; press Ctrl+O to expand it. To see which sessions Claude can reach, run /list-agents . Message another session Self-hosted environments v2.1.224 Self-hosted environments run Claude Code cloud sessions on your organization’s own infrastructure, in public beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Run claude self-hosted-runner on your machines or containers to turn them into runners. When someone picks your environment while starting a session from claude.ai, the mobile or desktop apps, or claude --cloud , that session runs inside your network, with access to your internal services. An Owner turns on Allow self-hosted environments in admin settings first. Signed in as an Owner, run the guided setup, which walks you through creating the environment and starts a runner: terminal claude self-hosted-runner setup The environment shows Healthy in admin settings once the runner registers. Self-hosted environments quickstart Auto mode becomes the default CLI Starting August 14, auto mode is the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. If you set a default mode yourself, it stays in place unless you accept the one-time switch prompt, and a default your organization manages doesn’t change. You can still switch modes at any time. Already in effect on those plans: the classifier calls auto mode makes no longer count toward your usage limits. To start every session in auto mode before the switch, set it as your default in your user settings: ~/.claude/settings.json { "permissions" : { "defaultMode" : "auto" } } New sessions then show auto mode on in the status bar. blogs.content: Week 30 · July 20–24, 2026 Copy page Copy page Opus 5 becomes the default Opus model, Claude Code Desktop adds an iOS Simulator pane, and the Claude Security plugin scans your code for vulnerabilities. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.214 → v2.1.219 3 features · July 20–24 Claude Opus 5 new model Claude Opus 5 is the new default Opus model in Claude Code. It’s the default on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and the Anthropic API, and on Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform. On the Anthropic API and on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, Opus 5 runs with a 1M-token context window ; on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, select the 1M model variant. Fast mode moves to Opus 5 at $10/$50 per MTok. Requires v2.1.219 or later. Switch to Opus 5 by name, or pick it from the model picker: Claude Code > /model claude-opus-5 Model configuration iOS Simulator in Claude Code Desktop Desktop Claude Code Desktop on macOS gets an iOS Simulator pane, in public beta on Pro, Max, and Team plans. When Claude builds, launches, or checks your app in a simulator, the pane opens next to the conversation and streams the device screen live, so you can watch Claude tap through the app to verify its changes or drive the device yourself. Requires Xcode with the iOS platform installed, and Claude Desktop v1.24012.0 or later. Ask Claude to run or test your app, and the pane opens when the app launches: Claude Code > Build the app and run it in the simulator to check the onboarding flow. Test iOS apps in the simulator Claude Security plugin plugin The Claude Security plugin runs a multi-agent vulnerability scan of your codebase inside a Claude Code session: agents map your architecture, build a threat model, hunt for vulnerabilities, and independently review every finding before writing the report to a CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ directory. Scan a whole repository or only a branch’s diff, a pull request, or a single commit, then turn the findings you choose into reviewed patches that you apply yourself. Install the plugin from the official Anthropic marketplace, run /reload-plugins , then start a scan with /claude-security : Claude Code > /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official Scan and fix your codebase Other wins /code-review now runs as a background subagent with its own context window, so review work stays out of your conversation and the findings arrive when it completes /verify , /code-review , and /deep-research run only when you invoke them; Claude no longer launches them on its own Emoji shortcodes autocomplete in the prompt input: type :heart: to insert an emoji, or two or more characters after : for suggestions; turn it off with emojiCompletionEnabled Skills with context: fork run in the background by default, and background: false in the skill’s frontmatter waits for the result in the same turn A session runs up to 20 subagents concurrently by default; change the limit with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS --max-budget-usd now enforces the cap on subagents: once spend reaches it, Claude can’t start more and running background subagents stop New sandbox.filesystem.disabled setting skips filesystem isolation while keeping network egress control In auto mode, the checks for dangerous rm commands, background jobs, and suspicious Windows paths no longer open permission dialogs; the auto-mode classifier adjudicates them instead Bash permission checks fail closed on more shell forms, including file-descriptor redirects, Zsh variable subscripts in [[ ]] comparisons, help and man invocations that could run unsafe options, and commands over 10,000 characters Fast mode no longer supports Opus 4.7: /fast now applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 Long-running tool calls emit a periodic progress heartbeat instead of going silent Full changelog for v2.1.214–v2.1.219 → Was this page helpful? blogs.description: 本文聚焦用 AI 写基金客户配置说明，常见四类走样：把业绩比较基准写成预期收益、年化与累计混用、漏写费率/最大回撤/赎回条件、只看风险等级就写“相匹配”。本文用一…
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 写基金配置说明：别把业绩比较基准写成预期收益 资讯 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月11日 本文聚焦用 AI 写基金客户配置说明，常见四类走样：把业绩比较基准写成预期收益、年化与累计混用、漏写费率/最大回撤/赎回条件、只看风险等级就写“相匹配”。本文用一个构造案例逐条拆解，给出六项必写清单、五问自检和一段可直接复制的提示词。 用 AI 写基金客户配置说明，常见四类走样：把业绩比较基准写成预期收益、年化与累计混用、漏写费率/最大回撤/赎回条件、只看风险等级就写“相匹配”。本文用一个构造案例逐条拆解，给出六项必写清单、五问自检和一段可直接复制的提示词。 周四下午，理财经理要给客户写一份配置说明。 客户风险测评为 C3 平衡型，本次准备投入 20 万元。这笔钱是孩子两年后上大学的学费，客户只提了一个要求：“稳一点。” 产品资料和客户档案一起交给 AI。它写得很快，四段话，条理清楚，还替客户算了一笔收益：持有一年，大约能拿到 2.48 万元。 问题不在文笔，而在于它把历史收益写成了未来结果，把业绩比较基准写成了收益预期，还把真正重要的客户约束留在了材料里。 一份基金客户配置说明，被改了七处 写配置说明，至少需要两类材料。 一类管“能说什么”，一类管“该不该说”。 材料 A｜产品要素与客户档案（节选） 产品：某混合型证券投资基金，风险等级 R3（中风险）。业绩比较基准：沪深 300 指数收益率 × 60% ＋ 中债综合全价指数收益率 × 40%。近一年收益率 12.4%，近三年年化收益率 5.8%，近三年最大回撤 -18.6%。管理费 1.2%/年，托管费 0.2%/年。赎回费：持有不满 7 天 1.5%，7 天至 1 年 0.5%，满 1 年免收。客户档案：风险测评 C3（平衡型），可承受最大回撤 15%，投资期限 2 年，本次投入 20 万元。客户原话（10-28 面谈）：这笔钱是孩子两年后上大学的学费，稳一点。 材料递过去后，AI 返回了下面这段初稿。 材料 B｜配置说明初稿（结论段） 该基金近一年收益 12.4%，年化回报约 12%，业绩比较基准为年化 8%，长期看有稳定的超额收益。产品风险等级 R3，与您的风险承受能力相匹配。建议本次投入 20 万元，持有一年可获得约 2.4 万元收益。该产品无封闭期，可随时赎回，流动性好。 逐条核对，至少能找出七处问题。 AI 写的 原始材料 问题 年化回报约 12% 近一年收益率 12.4%，近三年年化收益率 5.8% 混淆区间收益与年化口径 业绩比较基准为年化 8% 基准是由两个指数按权重组成的公式 擅自把基准换成数字 长期看有稳定的超额收益 材料没有提供足够依据 把有限历史表现外推为长期结论 持有一年可获得约 2.48 万元收益 20 万元 × 12.4%＝2.48 万元 算术成立，但把历史收益写成未来结果 与您的风险承受能力相匹配 客户可承受回撤 15%，产品近三年最大回撤 18.6% 只比较等级，忽略其他约束 无封闭期，可随时赎回 不同持有期限对应不同赎回费 把有条件赎回写成无条件流动性 未提费率和最大回撤 材料明确披露了相关数据 成本与风险信息缺失 照这份初稿发出去，客户最容易记住两个结论：一年能赚 2.48 万元，钱随时能取。 他未必会注意到，这只基金近三年曾出现 18.6% 的最大回撤。 20 万元的 18.6%，是 3.72 万元。最大回撤是历史指标，不代表未来损失的上限，也不构成收益或亏损预测。但它足以说明：这只产品的历史波动，已经超出客户档案中填写的承受范围。 而这 20 万元，是两年后的学费。 四类走样，越往后越难发现 配置说明不是写给同行看的，而是写给一个具体的人看的。 这个人不一定会计算年化收益，但一定会在亏钱时想起：你当初是怎么写的。 先要分清一个概念：业绩比较基准是衡量产品表现的参照，不是预期收益、目标收益，更不是收益承诺。产品可以跑赢它，也可以跑输它。 AI 写配置说明时，常见四类走样： 类别 通读能发现吗 原因 基准被说成收益 能 两个词不一样，写的人知道，读的人不知道 年化与累计混用 要算 数字看着都对，算法错 该写的没写 不能 删掉的东西没有痕迹 匹配只看等级 不能 等级相同，看起来就够了 基准被说成收益：两个词，两种责任 基准不能当成预期收益。它是参照线，收益是实际结果，两者之间没有承诺关系。写在一起，客户只记住后面那个数。 为什么会错。 模型嫌那串指数麻烦，会把它压成一个数。压完这一下，参照线就变成了收益承诺。「基准年化 8%」比一串指数好读，也好卖。 怎么核。 见到「基准」两个字，检查后面跟的是公式还是数字。跟数字的，一律改回公式，并补一句它只是参照。再核三处容易混的地方。 近一年、近三年、成立以来，三个区间不能互相替代。 年化、累计、区间收益，是三件事。 费前与费后，差的是每年 1.4 个百分点。 年化与累计：数字对，算法错 12.4% 本身就是年化。它是一年的收益，不必再折算。近三年的 5.8% 是折出来的：累计涨幅开三次方再减一。两个数都叫年化，含义差着一层。 为什么会错。 把一年的数写成「年化」，字面不算编造。但年化意味着每年都这样，客户听到的是一台稳定的机器。模型偏爱年化，因为年化是一个能写进句子的结论。 怎么核。 把每个百分数后面跟的区间词圈出来，缺的补上。再算一遍金额：20 万按 12.4% 是 2.48 万。数算得没错，错在把一个不确定的数当成可预期的数。 还有一个坑：算法不同。有的产品按单利演示，有的按复利折算。三年以内两者差得不多，五年以上会明显分开。银行理财、保险、信托的演示口径不一样，不能直接比。 该写的没写：必写的六项，缺一项就是缺 为什么会错。 删掉的东西没有痕迹，这是四类里唯一不靠句子就能发生的错。模型不会删掉费率，它根本不会写，因为没人要求它写。一份稿子里少了两行成本、少了一行回撤，读起来反而更顺。 怎么核。 别顺着稿子读，反过来查。把六项列成清单，逐项在稿子里找。 业绩基准 区间收益 最大回撤 管理费与托管费 赎回条件 风险提示 找不到的，就是缺的。材料里没有的，先补材料，不要让 AI 在文字上补。 费用也要按产品资料完整核对： 管理费、托管费等持续性费用； 申购费、赎回费等交易费用； 销售服务费等适用费用。 客户问“到手多少”，不能只看一个历史收益率，还要看实际适用的费用、持有期限和赎回安排。 风险等级相同，只算匹配的第一步 产品 R3，客户 C3，两个标签摆在一起，模型很容易写下“相匹配”。 但等级匹配不等于这份配置已经适合客户。至少还要问三个问题： 这笔钱多久不用？ 客户能承受多大的浮亏？ 这笔钱原本要做什么？ 本例中，不能只写“相匹配”： 客户可承受最大回撤为 15%，产品近三年最大回撤为 18.6%，两者存在需要提示的差异。 资金用途是学费，使用时间相对刚性，不能简单假设“亏了再多等几年”。 投资期限只有两年，材料也没有提供足够信息，证明出现回撤后一定能在资金使用前修复。 等级只是档案里的一个字段。期限和用途，往往只出现在客户面谈中，却最能决定一份建议是否稳妥。 基金配置说明怎么写：把两张表并排放，再动笔 顺序错了，后面全是补救。 先写再核，核出来的问题容易在下一轮改写中被“润色”掉。先把产品要素和客户约束并排放好，很多话一开始就不该出现。 第一步：把产品要素和客户约束各列一张表。 产品表至少包括六项：业绩比较基准、区间收益、最大回撤、费率、赎回、等级。客户表至少包括四行：风险等级、投资期限、可承受回撤、资金用途。 把两张表放在同一屏上。哪里对不上，先标出来，不要急着用一句“整体匹配”盖过去。 第二步：让每句事实性结论都有来源。 来源可以是产品资料，也可以是客户档案。 挂不上来源的句子，要么是模型补的，要么是撰写者自己希望成立的。两种都不应直接进入正文。 这一步看起来笨，却能把“我觉得合适”，换成“材料里明确写着”。 第三步：用清单反查缺失，再检查语气 六项逐一打勾，缺一项补一项。补不出来时，先判断是漏写，还是原始材料不足。 最后把客户原话放回去读一遍。 如果客户说的是“这笔钱两年后要用，稳一点”，正文却写着“持有一年可获得约 2.48 万元”，问题就不只是措辞不准确，而是整份说明偏离了客户真正的约束。 可直接复制的提示词 你是财富管理岗的配置说明撰写助手。本次只做一件事：用我给的两张表，写一份给客户看的配置说明。 表一（产品要素）：业绩基准、区间收益、最大回撤、费率、赎回条件、风险等级。 表二（客户约束）：风险等级、投资期限、可承受回撤、资金用途。 请遵守以下规则： 1. 业绩比较基准必须按原文披露，不得擅自换算或简化，不得写成预期收益、目标收益或收益承诺； 2. 每个收益率必须保留原始区间和计算口径，例如“近一年收益率”“近三年年化收益率”。不得把历史收益外推为未来收益； 3. 不得出现任何金额化的收益预测，包括「持有一年可赚 X 元」； 4. 费率、最大回撤、赎回条件三项必须出现在正文，缺一项视为未完成。 匹配结论只写事实：产品等级、客户等级、期限、可承受回撤，四项并排陈述，由客户自己判断是否接受。 写法要求：一段一件事；每句不超过三十字；每个结论后面注明来自表一还是表二。 输出两部分：配置说明初稿；两表之间对不上的地方（单列清单，不要自行调和）。 如果团队已经在使用 AutoClaw，可以把资料对齐、逐句标注来源和缺失检查交给它辅助完成。对不上的地方应单列，不要自动调和。至于该不该推荐、如何向客户解释，仍需人来判断。 改完，用五个问题过一遍。 每个百分数后面，都跟着一个区间词吗？ 业

blogs.title: AI 会议纪要准确吗？业绩说明会纪要最该核对的 4 类内容
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: 本文指出：AI 会议纪要只能当“索引”，不能当“记录”，不能直接抄用或外发；最该核数字与单位、限定词、说话人、时间口径四类内容，做法是存好底稿、让 AI 列清单而非…
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 会议纪要准确吗？业绩说明会纪要最该核对的 4 类内容 资讯 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月11日 本文指出：AI 会议纪要只能当“索引”，不能当“记录”，不能直接抄用或外发；最该核数字与单位、限定词、说话人、时间口径四类内容，做法是存好底稿、让 AI 列清单而非写总结、只核四个字段并五问自检；涉未同意录音、客户敏感信息、直接对外材料三种场合不宜使用，应走人工或合规流程。 摘要： AI 会议纪要适合当“索引”，不适合当“记录”。用于业绩说明会、电话会议纪要时，最容易出错的是四类内容：数字与单位、限定词、说话人、时间口径。本文给出每类的典型错法、核对方法，以及三步核对流程和五问自检清单。 业绩说明会结束两小时后，AI 纪要已经发到你的邮箱。你扫了一遍：句子通顺，数字带单位，“管理层表示”也写得有模有样。你把其中一句抄进跟踪笔记。第二天，同事问你：这句话是管理层说的，还是提问的人说的？ 你回去翻逐字稿，发现问题不止一个： 原话：我们争取 把全年毛利率维持在 48% 到 49% 。 纪要：全年毛利率将 维持在 49% 。 区间变成了一个点，“争取”变成了“将”。一个打算，被写成了一个承诺。对研究公司的人来说，这是两条完全不同的信息。 AI 会议纪要能用，但只能当“索引”，不能当“记录” ：它告诉你该回去看哪几段，但不能直接抄进笔记，更不能直接发出去。为什么会这样、哪四类内容最该核、具体怎么核，下面分别说。 一、AI 会议纪要为什么不能当记录 AI 出纪要确实快。一场一个半小时的电话会，逐字稿约两万字。人工整理要半天，AI 只要几分钟。这一点不用怀疑。 但要分清两样东西： 逐字稿是记录。它记下谁、在什么时候、说了什么，一个字不改，可以引用。 纪要是索引。它从两万字里挑出几百字，告诉你哪里值得回去看，只能用来查找。 AI 纪要的麻烦在于，它长得像记录：句子完整，有结论，有数字表，看起来可以直接转发。 可它其实做了大量取舍。而模型并不知道金融材料里哪些字更重要。比如它不知道： “争取”两个字，比一个形容词重要得多； 分析师提问里的数字，不能算成管理层说的； 单季数据和全年指引，不能放进同一句话。 模型更倾向于保留“看起来像结论”的内容。所以错误不是随机的，而是集中在四类内容上。 二、四类最该核的内容 下表先给出全貌。四类按“错了之后有多难发现”从易到难排列。 表 1｜四类内容：纪要怎么写错、当场怎么核 类别 原话 纪要容易写成 怎么核 1. 数字与单位 资本开支 1,900 亿元 1.9 万亿 回到原句，连同单位、币种一起核 2. 限定词 原则上不再新增产能，除非订单确认 不再新增产能 搜“争取、原则上、预计”等词 3. 说话人 分析师：市场预期 12 亿 管理层提到 12 亿 查这个数最先由谁说出 4. 时间口径 单季增 15%；全年指引不变 营收增 15%，全年目标翻倍 给每个数标上期间 第 1 类：数字与单位——数值没变，量级变了 例子：管理层说“全年资本开支预计 1,900 亿元”，纪要写成“1.9 万亿”。差了十倍。 更常见的错没这么显眼： “毛利率提升 2 个百分点”，写成“提升 2%”； “亿元”的一列数，按“万元”抄进了表； “同比”写成了“环比”； 港股、中概股电话会里，美元、港元、人民币混着说，纪要只留下了数字。 为什么会错：AI 知道“这里有个数字”，但不知道它对应哪张表、用什么单位。数字通常不是编的，而是在搬运时掉了东西。 怎么核：回到逐字稿找到原句，检查四样东西：数值、单位、币种、比较基准。少一样就以原稿为准。如果公司同时发了业绩公告，再对一次原表。 第 2 类：限定词——删掉的往往是最要紧的字 例子：原话是“原则上不再新增产能，除非下游订单确认”，纪要写成“不再新增产能”。 一个有条件的打算，变成了一个已定的决策。再往下传一手，它就可能被当成公司的承诺。 为什么会错：摘要追求简洁。“争取”“原则上”“预计”这类词让句子变长、变犹豫，模型就倾向于删掉它们。它优化的是流畅，不是准确。 怎么核：很简单。在逐字稿和纪要里分别搜这几个词：争取、原则上、预计、需审批、不超过、如果。 如果逐字稿里有七处“预计”，纪要里一处都没有，说明条件被删光了。 这一类反而最常被漏掉。因为数字错了你会觉得“不对劲”，限定词没了，你只会觉得“写得真干脆”。 为什么这在金融场景格外重要： 上市公司在投资者关系活动中的发言，本身受监管约束。 正因为有这些限制，管理层说话时常用“争取”“预计”“不给具体指引”来留余地。纪要把这些词删掉，等于替公司说了一句它按规定不能说的话。 第 3 类：说话人——分析师的问题，变成了管理层的回答 例子： 分析师： 市场预期全年利润 12 亿，你们怎么看？ 管理层： 我们不给出具体指引。 纪要： 管理层提到全年利润 12 亿。 数字是真的，但说话人错了。更糟的是，管理层那句“不给指引”被删掉了。纪要传达的意思，正好和会上发生的事相反。 为什么这类错误要紧： “谁说的”决定了这句话的性质。管理层说的是公司口径；分析师说的只是市场猜测。两者能不能写进笔记、能不能引用，标准完全不同。 为什么难发现：句子完整，没有错字，读多少遍都看不出问题。 怎么核：凡是带数字的“管理层表示”，都回到问答原段，确认这个数最先是谁说的。 还要注意一点：转写工具标的说话人，本身也可能标错。多人会议、电话串线时尤其常见。标签和上下文对不上时，以录音为准。 第 4 类：时间口径——每个数都对，但不属于同一期 这是最难发现的一类，因为没有一个数字是错的。 例子： 会上管理层先后说了四句话： 三季度营收同比增长 15%； 上年同期基数较低； 全年指引维持不变； 未来三年目标翻倍。 纪要把它们压成一句：“营收增长 15%，全年目标翻倍。” 每个数字都能在逐字稿里找到，但它们分属不同的时间段，不能放在一句话里推出结论。 金融材料里最容易混的两处： 单季还是累计？A 股季报同时列示“本报告期”和“年初至报告期末”两组数据。管理层说“三季度增长 15%”，可能指单季，也可能指前三季度累计。纪要往往只留下数字。 “全年”是哪一年？A 股公司的会计年度是公历年度。但不少港股、美股公司的财年不从 1 月开始。纪要里的“全年”，要确认对应哪个财年。 怎么核：给纪要里的每个数字标上期间，然后问自己：这一句里的几个数，是同一期的吗？ 三、具体怎么核：三步走 不用换工具，也不用放弃 AI 纪要。只需要换一下它在流程里的位置： 纪要不是最终成品，而是帮你找原文的索引。 第一步：先把材料存下来。 保存录音、逐字稿和公司发布的材料，记下时间和版本。业绩说明会有时会发更正材料，没有固定版本，后面就没法核。 如果是 A 股公司，还可以看看公司有没有在交易所互动平台或业绩说明会平台发布投资者关系活动记录或文字实录。它可以用来对照，但它也是公司整理过的版本，不等于逐字稿。 第二步：让 AI 列清单，不要让它写总结。 不要“五条要点”。要让 AI 把所有带数字、带条件、带承诺的句子逐条列成表，每条注明四项： 原话 说话人 在逐字稿中的位置 说的是已发生的事，还是对未来的判断 这样的表格没有总结好看，但每一行都能对回原文。好看和能核是两回事，研究公司材料需要的是能核。 第三步：只核四个字段。 单位与量级、限定词、说话人、时间期间。其他措辞不必逐字改。 核完后，用下面五个问题自检： 每个带单位的数字，都在逐字稿里找到了原句，单位和币种一致吗？ 搜过“争取、原则上、预计、需审批、不超过”吗？该留的条件还在吗？ 每个带数字的“管理层表示”，都确认过是谁先说的吗？ 同一句里的几个数字，都属于同一期吗？ 纪要末尾写明材料的版本和时间了吗？别人能照着再核一遍吗？ 五条都过，纪要可以放进工作底稿。有一条没过，先别往外发。 AutoClaw 能帮哪一步：你可以把逐字稿和公司材料交给 AutoClaw，让它按第二步的字段拆出一张核对表，以表格或文档交付。它不会判断哪句话算承诺，也不会替你下结论。表里每一行，仍需要你对回原稿确认。判断和签字，留在你这一侧。 四、哪些场合不要用 AI 纪要 以下三种情况，核对方法也不够用。应当由人记录，或先走所在机构的合规流程。 1. 没有取得录音同意，或机构不允许录音的会议。 能合法录音、合规存放，是一切的前提。这比纪要准不准更先要回答。 2. 涉及客户身份、账户、持仓或未公开信息的沟通。 材料一旦传进第三方工具，就多了一份副本。纪要里也不该出现这些信息。 另外，如果你在核对中发现某句话在公司公开文件里找不到依据，而且可能影响股价，不要把它当“独家信息”记下来，应按所在机构的合规流程处理。 3. 需要直接对外发出的材料。 纪要可以进工作底稿，但不宜直接变成给客户的文件、研报依据或公开引用。中间那道人工确认不能省。 最后提醒一句：转写准确率受录音质量、说话人数、口音和专业术语影响，各家统计口径也不同。 不写明口径的准确率数字，不要拿来选工具。 AI 可以把两万字压成几百字，但它不能替你决定哪几个字不能丢。纪要末尾那句“已核对”，仍然要你自己写。 本文讨论会议纪要的核对方法，不构成投资建议或合规意见，也不评价任何具体产品。文中例句与数字均为构造样例，不对应真实公司、会议或披露文件。

Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.158 → v2.1.165 4 features · June 1–5 Auto mode on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry v2.1.158 Auto mode is now available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry for Opus 4.7 and Opus 4.8, replacing permission prompts with background safety checks on third-party providers. Opt in by setting CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 . Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.139 → v2.1.142 3 features · May 11–15 Agent view research preview claude agents opens one screen for every Claude Code session: what’s running, what’s blocked on your input, and what’s done. Dispatch a bug fix, a pull request review, and a flaky-test investigation as three rows, keep working in another window, and step in only when a row needs you. Attach to any row to drop into its full conversation, then press ← to return to the list. Each background session keeps running without a terminal attached. Open the dashboard from your shell: terminal claude agents Agent view /goal v2.1.139 Set a completion condition and Claude keeps working toward it across turns without you prompting each step. After every turn, a fast model checks whether the condition holds; if not, Claude starts another turn instead of handing control back. Useful for substantial work with a verifiable end state, like migrating a module until every call site compiles and tests pass. The goal clears once the condition is met, and works in interactive, -p , and Remote Control. Set a goal and let Claude run until it holds: Claude Code > /goal all tests in test/auth pass and the lint step is clean Goals Fast mode on Opus 4.7 research preview /fast now runs on Opus 4.7 by default instead of Opus 4.6. Fast mode is a high-speed Opus configuration: the same model quality at about 2.5x the speed for a higher per-token cost, useful for rapid iteration and live debugging. Pricing is unchanged at $30/$150 per MTok, the same as Opus 4.6 fast mode. To pin fast mode to Opus 4.6, set CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE=1 . blogs.content: Week 13 · March 23–27, 2026 Copy page Copy page Auto mode for hands-off permissions, computer use built in, PR auto-fix in the cloud, transcript search, and a PowerShell tool for Windows. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.83 → v2.1.85 6 features · March 23–27 Auto mode research preview Auto mode hands your permission prompts to a classifier. Safe edits and commands run without interrupting you; anything destructive or suspicious gets blocked and surfaced. It’s the middle ground between approving every file write and running with --dangerously-skip-permissions . Cycle to auto with Shift+Tab, or set it as your default: ~/.claude/settings.json { "permissions" : { "defaultMode" : "auto" } } Permission modes guide Computer use Desktop Claude can now control your actual desktop from the Claude Code Desktop app: open native apps, click through the iOS simulator, drive hardware control panels, and verify changes on screen. It’s off by default and asks before each action. Best for the things nothing else can reach: apps without an API, proprietary tools, anything that only exists as a GUI. Enable it in Settings, grant the OS permissions, then ask Claude to verify a change end to end: Claude Code Open the iOS simulator, tap through the onboarding flow, and screenshot each step Computer use guide PR auto-fix Web Flip a switch when you open a PR and walk away. Claude watches CI, fixes the failures, handles the nits, and pushes until it’s green. No more babysitting a PR through six rounds of lint errors. After creating a PR on Claude Code web, toggle Auto fix in the CI panel. Auto-fix pull requests Transcript search v2.1.83 Press / in transcript mode to search your conversation. n and N step through matches. Finally a way to find that one Bash command Claude ran 400 messages ago. Open transcript mode and search: Claude Code Ctrl+O # open transcript /migrate # search for "migrate" n # next match N # previous match Fullscreen guide PowerShell tool preview v2.1.84 Windows gets a native PowerShell tool alongside Bash. Claude can run cmdlets, pipe objects, and work with Windows-native paths without translating everything through Git Bash. blogs.title: AI 生成的 PPT 怎么修改？三层修改法减少整份重做
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: AI 生成的 PPT 每提一次意见就整份重做，是因为三类修改混在一起；按大纲、论点、样式分三层下达，改动只落在该动的页面。附可复用的修改清单。
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 生成的 PPT 怎么修改？三层修改法减少整份重做 教程 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月9日 AI 生成的 PPT 每提一次意见就整份重做，是因为三类修改混在一起；按大纲、论点、样式分三层下达，改动只落在该动的页面。附可复用的修改清单。 改 AI 生成的 PPT：减少整份重做的三层修改法 "把第 5 页的结论放大""整体风格再正式一点""第 3 页的数据换成最新的"——三条意见提完，AI 把整份 PPT 重新生成了一遍。改完之后对照原文件：第 1 页的标题换了说法，第 4、5 页的表述全部重写，连"需要的支持"都变成了"Q4 展望"。三条意见只想动两个页面，结果牵连了全部五页。 很多返工发生在意见下达的方式上：三条意见落在三个不同的层面——页面结构、单页内容、全稿外观——却以一句模糊指令一起发给了 AI。AI 唯一安全的回应是把整份文件当作整体重新产出，于是每一次修改都是一次重做。本文不把这种现象归咎于工具，而是通过一次分三层的对照修改，说明怎样让改动只落在该落的地方。 让 AI 精准修改的关键，不是把意见写得更客气，而是先分层、再锁层、最后逐页下达：大纲层先锁定，论点层逐页替换，样式层一次统一。 1. AI 整份重做，会连没人提的页面一起改掉 为了把这件事量清楚，我们做了一次对照修改：同一份脚本生成的 5 页演示 PPT（第三季度经营汇报，内容为演示材料），同样三条意见，用两种方式各改一遍。条件 A 把三条意见一次性下达并整份重做；条件 B 先判定每条意见的层——数字放大属于论点层且只涉及第 2 页，风格属于样式层，原因表述属于第 3 页的论点层——然后逐层、逐页修改。 比对口径只有一条：一页算"被改"，指该页任何一处文本与基准逐字不同；字号、字体、颜色这类样式属性的变化单独记录。逐页比对由脚本读取两版文件的全部文字完成，不靠肉眼。 条件 A 的结果是 5 页文本全部变化。被意见指向的第 2、3 页都按意见落实了，但第 1 页的标题被改写成"Q3 经营汇报（整理版）"，第 4 页"待观察：交付率是否在 11 月继续回升"被改写成"交付率回升情况待 11 月数据验证"，第 5 页"需要的支持：增补一名数据分析师"变成了"Q4 展望"——这三页没有任何意见指向它们。条件 B 的结果是仅第 3 页文本变化：第 2 页文字逐字未动、字号从 18 磅放大到 30 磅，第 3 页表述替换为最新说法，全稿字体统一为黑体，未被指向的第 1、4、5 页逐字未动。 两种条件对照的结论很直接：整份重做会让意见范围之外的页面跟着变化，分三层下达则把改动限制在了意见指向的位置。原因也不复杂——模糊指令下执行者无法只改局部，唯一稳妥的做法就是把文件当作整体重新产出，而重新产出意味着每一页的文字都会被重新组织。 2. 判断意见在哪一层，每条问一句话 把意见分层，用三个问句就能判定：这条意见动的是页面顺序和"每页回答什么问题"吗——是，就属于大纲层；动的是某页的结论、数据或证据吗——是，就属于论点层；动的是颜色、字体、版式吗——是，就属于样式层。一条意见同时涉及两层的情况（比如"第 5 页换个更正式的说法，再配张图"），拆成两条分别处理。 层 判定问句 对应的意见示例 大纲层 动的是页面顺序和"每页回答什么问题"吗 前面加一页预算、第 4 页和第 6 页合并 论点层 动的是某页的结论、数据或证据吗 第 5 页结论放大、数据换成最新月份 样式层 动的是颜色、字体、版式吗 风格再正式一点、字太小、配色换成公司色 分层的执行顺序是固定的：大纲层最先锁定。大纲牵动全局——加一页，后面的页码全部顺移；合并两页，两页的论点要重新组织。大纲的验收标准是每一页都能用一句话说出它在回答什么问题，整份文件没有重复回答同一问题的页面；锁定后明确说"大纲就按这个定了"，再进入论点层。 论点层逐页执行，意见带页码、带元素、带来源。"整体再丰富一点"要改写成"第 5 页结论后面，补一张本月与上月的对比数据，数据来自销售系统本月导出"——前者让 AI 猜在哪页补什么，后者没有猜测空间。凡是涉及数据的页面，改完后要回原始表格核对一遍数值和口径。 样式层最后一次性执行。逐条零散改样式的效率很低，还容易改出不一致——同一级标题在不同页里出现两种字号。先把样式意见汇总成规则清单（标题字号与颜色、正文字体、强调方式、页码位置），再交给 AI 一次执行全稿，有品牌规范的对照品牌规范执行。 3. 三条意见，改成一段可以执行的修改指令 下面用开头那三条意见演示如何分层下达。这次拆解用于说明指令的写法，不是 A/B 测试，也不代表拆层后一定减少多少轮修改。 原始要求："把第 5 页的结论放大""整体风格再正式一点""第 3 页的数据换成最新的"。 分层改写后的指令： 请按以下清单修改这份 PPT，只动清单列出的位置，其余页面逐字保留。 样式层（全稿）：标题字号 28 号、深蓝色；正文字体不变；强调色只用公司模板的深红。 论点层（第 5 页）：结论字号放大到 32 号；结论行下方补一行数据出处。 论点层（第 3 页）：原因表述替换为最新口径，替换后其余文字逐字保留。 这段指令并不复杂，但它提前回答了 AI 最容易猜错的三个问题：改哪几层、动哪些页、哪些内容不能动。更重要的是"只动清单列出的位置"这一句，把修改的范围和验收标准同时给到了——执行完成后，未被点到的页面逐字未动，就是这次修改合格的标志。 如果这类修改任务经常出现，可以把基准文件和这张清单一起交给 AutoClaw 这样的工具：输入是基准文件、分层后的意见清单和比对口径，输出是修改后的文件和逐页比对记录。这里强调的是下达方法，不对工具在所有场景下的表现作未经验证的承诺。 可复用的空白修改清单： 意见 层 页码 下达写法 落实与核对 4. 修改完成后，先看没人提的页面动没动 即使清单写得很完整，执行结果也要验收。更稳定的做法不是通读一遍看感觉，而是先按清单定位检查：被点到的页面是否按意见落实，落实的方式是否改变了其他内容，被禁止改动的部分有没有被碰到。 如果被点到的页改对了、其余页面逐字未动，这次修改就可以交付；如果未点到的页面出现了变化，先查是哪条意见的执行溢出了范围，把溢出的部分退回——而不是接受一个"大体没问题"的版本。验收时至少检查三件事：数据页的数值和口径是否与原始材料一致；版式规则是否全稿一致；未被点到的页面是否真的没有被碰到。 对于法律、财务、医疗、隐私或对外承诺等内容，还需要相关人员人工复核。让 AI 精准修改并不意味着追求零沟通，更现实的目标是把范围和标准前置：清单给足边界，验收守住边界。

blogs.author: Kimi

blogs.content: Kimi 发布游戏开发与创意工作解决方案 联系销售团队 下载 Kimi 桌面端 今天， Kimi 发布「游戏开发与创意工作解决方案」。 基于 Kimi K3.1 系列模型、Kimi Code 与 Kimi Work 系列 Agent 产品，以及 Unity、Unreal Engine、Blender 等专业工具插件，我们希望帮助游戏团队更快验证玩法创意、推进工程和美术制作，并将发行与运营中的玩家反馈带回下一轮迭代。 游戏创意的价值，往往要到玩家真正操作时才能判断： 策划文档能说明规则，却难以回答操作是否顺手、奖励是否明确、节奏是否吸引人。若这些问题在关卡、代码和资产大量完成后才暴露，调整就会牵动更多人和预算。 Kimi 希望帮助团队尽早做出范围明确的可玩版本，再根据真实体验决定如何投入。 游戏行业的业务挑战：更快验证，也要稳定交付 游戏开发的第一道门槛，是创意验证的成本 。 一个玩法是否有趣，需要真正玩起来才能判断。但制作原型需要投入时间和人力，团队往往只能优先验证少数想法。如何降低单次尝试的成本，在有限时间内验证更多创意？ Unity《2026 Game Development Report》 显示，52% 的受访开发者优先选择小规模项目来降低风险，67% 将原型阶段控制在三个月以内。更审慎的研发投入、更紧凑的验证周期，让原型制作效率变得更加重要。 Kimi 游戏解决方案，可以帮助游戏团队高效制作项目原型，在有限时间内探索和比较更多玩法方向，从而做出更准确的业务判断。 第二道门槛，来自跨岗位和跨工具的协作 。策划需求，需要变成工程任务；美术资产，也需要符合引擎规范。AI 若只生成一段文字或一张图，仍需要团队花大量时间进行适配和创作，才能搬进原有流程。 Kimi 解决方案可以直接衔接团队现有的工作流，操作专业工具与编辑器、修改现有工程，并交付可继续编辑的文件和清晰的操作记录，方便团队审阅、协作和推进后续工作。 Kimi 游戏开发与创意工作解决方案：从创意落地到持续迭代 Kimi 可以从团队的实际目标出发，推动创意从设想走向实践。 例如，策划想验证「在三消玩法中加入可自由组合的规则卡」是否有趣，但仅凭玩法说明，很难感受规则叠加后带来的策略变化。Kimi 会围绕这一目标，梳理规则卡的组合方式及其对消除策略、得分与反馈的影响，再将其拆解为交互、数值、界面和视听等具体制作任务，制作可试玩的原型。 这样，策划、开发和美术就能围绕同一个原型，边玩边讨论，减少创意在沟通与交接中的理解偏差。 结合模型能力与专业工具，Kimi 还可以将这种工作方式的变化，延伸到游戏开发、制作等更多环节。 模型能力与插件支持 一个游戏项目往往横跨多个团队，涉及策划文档、截图、代码、3D 资产等多种项目文件。 Kimi 可以为这一复杂流程提供支持：模型负责理解这些输入并规划、执行任务； Kimi Code 支持面向代码库中的实现和修改； Kimi Work 可以承接跨文件、跨步骤的制作任务。团队可以在这些成果的基础上继续完善，衔接后续制作流程。 针对不同团队的需求，我们也提供了覆盖日常办公、代码开发与 API 集成的系列产品，供大家选择： 此外，Kimi 还可通过插件与工具调用连接 Blender、Unity、Unreal Engine 等专业软件，直接操作现有工程，协助完成游戏开发与 3D 创作等任务。 正式立项前：用 Godot 把想法做成可试玩原型 游戏立项前，团队往往需要快速验证新玩法，但开发资源未必充足。 借助 Kimi，缺少编程经验的策划或创意团队也能在 1–2 天内做出可试玩原型。先验证玩法，再决定是否投入。 比如，团队想制作一款 2.5D 动作游戏的原型，可以提供参考图和视频，说明预期的场景氛围与玩法机制。Kimi 通过多模态能力理解参考素材中的关键视觉元素，再使用 Godot 游戏引擎搭建可试玩 Demo，呈现雨夜光影、地面积水和灯笼等场景细节，并实现挥剑、闪避和格挡等核心玩法。 制作过程中，Kimi 还可以实际运行游戏，结合渲染画面和试玩录像，检查视觉效果与功能是否达到要求。发现问题后，自主修改并重新验证，在交付前完成多轮迭代，让团队拿到的首个版本更接近预期。 有了可试玩原型，团队就能围绕实际体验展开评审：雨夜中的战斗辨识度、挥剑打击感，以及闪避与格挡的攻防体验。 团队可以据此不断调整和复测，验证核心玩法是否成立，再决定是否扩展关卡与敌人类型。 美术资产适配：让 Blender 资产从概念走向游戏场景 美术资产进入游戏场景，要经过比概念呈现更严格的检查：角色多视角是否一致，模型有无穿插，纹理和隐藏文字是否有缺陷，资源规格能否满足引擎预算。 Kimi 可以协助完成上述检查与初步调整：模型通过多模态理解，结合多视角视频与截图判断空间关系，发现并定位比例、穿插和材质问题；再将调整方案转化为脚本，借助本地 Agent 操作专业软件，完成初步修改。 通过 Blender 插件，Kimi 可以直接操作软件，协助美术团队搭建、预览和修改场景。 团队既可以提供现有工程与资产，让它完成摆放、组合和布局调整；也可以提供参考图片或视频，附上制作要求，让它从零建模、组装资产并搭建场景，还原参考中的整体形态与空间布局。 以建筑场景为例，根据美术团队提供的资产或参考图片及制作要求，Kimi 会在软件里先确定建筑的整体形态与空间布局，再逐步完善结构、材质和灯光；复杂建筑则拆分为不同构件，分步搭建与细化。搭建过程中，通过多视角预览检查模型比例、穿插与材质表现，及时发现并修正问题，提升首版交付的完成度与质量。美术团队可在此基础上继续打磨，把握最终风格与质量，将更多精力投入设计判断与细节表现，减少基础搭建和反复排查的工作量。 Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Blender 构建了一座机场室内雨林山谷场景，并制作了一段 17.5 秒、1920×1080 分辨率、60 fps 的 3D 建模展示视频。使用工具：Blender、Python、Geometry Nodes（几何节点）、Cycles（渲染引擎）、Pillow、NumPy 和 FFmpeg。使用的外部素材：来自 Poly Haven 的 4K HDRI 环境贴图 “Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)”，由 Greg Zaal 和 Jarod Guest 创作，采用 CC0 许可协议，用于天空照明和环境反射。 Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个可交互的、基于浏览器的 3D 体验，打造了一座大教堂的内部场景。该场景约包含 330 万个三角面，并为 8,368 个组件制作了动画效果，呈现出肋拱穹顶、石雕塑像，以及色彩鲜明的彩绘玻璃光影。使用的外部素材：来自 Poly Haven 的石材纹理（CC0 许可）；Mylius 拍摄的彩绘玻璃照片（CC BY-SA 3.0 许可）。 游戏开发：把 Agent 带入 Unity 与 Unreal Engine 的现有工程 进入正式开发后，团队面对的是已有工程、既定架构和不断变化的需求。 一个看似简单的功能，可能同时影响角色状态、界面、存档和关卡逻辑；一个完整的 3D 场景，也要兼顾空间关系、视觉效果、物理交互与运行性能。工程越复杂，模块之间的依赖越多，问题就越难定位和解决。 面对这类牵一发而动全身的工程问题，Kimi 可以在获得工程文件和必要权限后，先梳理代码结构、场景层级和模块依赖，找到真正需要修改的位置，再借助插件在 Unity、Unreal Engine 等编辑器中完成具体操作。 改动完成后，Kimi 会结合问题复现、日志和运行数据验证效果，并根据结果继续调整。交付时保留代码差异和验证记录，方便工程师检查功能、性能与兼容性。 围绕这套工作流程，我们在内部探索了几类用法： Kimi + Unity：从网页试玩走向专业开发。 可玩 Demo 只是开始，要走向正式上线，还需进一步完善工程，以支撑后续的调试、打磨与持续迭代。Kimi 模型与 Unity 中国推出的游戏开发智能体 Tuanjie Codely Agent 及 团结引擎协同 ，将需求理解、工程实现与测试迭代串联起来：Kimi 模型负责理解开发者的创作意图与游戏设计、生成实现代码，并根据录屏与测试结果分析问题、制定修改方案；Tuanjie Codely Agent 则依托与团结引擎的原生整合，通过 Editor / Runtime Script 等方式直接在引擎中执行操作，完成场景搭建、玩法实现、工程修改与运行验证。 开发流程由此从“人提需求—模型写代码—人来操作”，延伸为“模型理解与生成—Agent 操作引擎—模型分析反馈—Agent 修改工程并验证”的完整闭环，减少了开发者在工具间切换与手动操作的成本。 在一次演示中，Kimi 在没有人工干预的情况下连续工作 20 小时，不仅复现了原作，还产出了一份可持续开发的原生工程，为后续玩法扩展、画面打磨及多端适配打下基础。 Kimi + Unreal Engine：跨模块的玩法开发与联调。 游戏玩法的新增或调整，往往会同时牵动角色行为、动画、物理效果和界面反馈。开发者提供相关脚本、组件配置与预期效果后，Kimi 可以梳理各模块之间的调用关系，协助修改代码、补充日志与测试，并结合 Unreal Engine blogs.description: GLM-5.3 与 GLM-5.3-Flash 是分工不是替代：高频轻量任务用 Flash，复杂长程工程用旗舰，附任务分配标准与组合用法。
blogs.content: 返回博客 GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 有什么区别？能力对比与场景选型 模型 作者：AutoClaw 2026年11月6日 GLM-5.3 与 GLM-5.3-Flash 是分工不是替代：高频轻量任务用 Flash，复杂长程工程用旗舰，附任务分配标准与组合用法。 GLM-5.3 和 GLM-5.3-Flash 有什么区别？能力对比与场景选型 同一个任务，用 GLM-5.3 跑还是用 GLM-5.3-Flash 跑，差别不在"谁更聪明"，而在"这个任务值不值得动用旗舰"。一句话给结论：高频、轻量、要快速反馈的日常工作，用 GLM-5.3-Flash；需要较少人工拆解、持续时间长、结果要求高的复杂任务，交给 GLM-5.3。两者是分工关系，不是替代关系——本文按官网公开口径把两者的能力、定位和适用场景讲清楚，帮你在 AutoClaw 里把任务分对模型。 先看速览：一屏分清两个模型 维度 GLM-5.3-Flash GLM-5.3 定位 GLM-5 系列首个原生多模态模型，面向高效编程与长程 Agent 任务 面向复杂工程与长程 Agent 任务的最新旗舰 架构特点 稀疏注意力与线性注意力混合架构，保持长上下文的同时显著降低计算开销 旗舰级 Agentic Coding，复杂工程与长程任务 在 AutoClaw 中的角色 高频、轻量、需要及时反馈的日常工作 需要较少人工拆解、持续时间更长、结果要求更高的任务 典型任务 截图理解、信息整理、文档处理、快速迭代 大型代码库、端到端开发、深度调试、长程研究 相对上一代 在多项基准与实际任务中超越 GLM-5.2 旗舰定位，承担最重的任务 维度一：定位不同，一个管快，一个管深 GLM-5.3-Flash 的关键词是"原生多模态 + 低开销"。它是 GLM-5 系列首个原生多模态模型，采用稀疏注意力与线性注意力混合架构，在保持精准长上下文能力的同时显著降低计算开销——翻译成使用体验：响应快、成本低、看得了图，适合一天要跑很多轮的工作。"原生多模态"意味着看图不是外挂能力：截图、图表、扫描件、设计稿这些视觉输入直接进模型理解，不用先转成文字描述再喂进去，中间环节的信息损失就此消失。 GLM-5.3 的关键词是"旗舰 + 长程"。它不只擅长生成代码，更能在大型项目中持续理解目标、处理多步骤依赖、使用工具并根据执行结果不断调整——从分析问题到执行、验证和交付，完整推进整个工作过程。这类任务的共同点是：中途不能断、步骤之间有依赖、错了要能自己排查着改。一个需求从设计、实现走到测试修复，中间任何一个环节断了都要重来的，就是它该接的活。混合架构对 Flash 的意义同样值得说透：长文档、长对话之所以在传统架构上又慢又贵，是因为注意力的计算量随长度暴涨；稀疏与线性注意力混合之后，长上下文仍然精准，但每个 token 的开销显著下降——这就是"又长又快"能同时成立的技术原因。 维度二：在 AutoClaw 里，它们分别接什么活 AutoClaw 支持模型切换（GLM 系列、DeepSeek 系列），两个模型的分工在官网模型页写得非常明确。GLM-5.3-Flash 适合处理图片、截图和视觉文档理解，图表、文件和信息的快速整理，文档、报告与内容处理，以及高频、多步骤的日常工作流——凡是需要快速反馈和持续迭代的任务，都是它的主场。 GLM-5.3 则面向复杂软件工程与大型代码库，从需求到实现的端到端开发，深度调试、代码重构与问题排查，多工具、多步骤工作流，以及长时间运行的研究和技术任务。它处理的是那些"中途不能断、错了要自己排查"的硬任务。 实际使用里还有第三种用法：同一任务的两个阶段用不同模型。比如一份长报告，先让 GLM-5.3 搭好结构和关键论证，再用 GLM-5.3-Flash 快速迭代格式、补图表、改措辞——重活在旗舰上做，轻改在 Flash 上跑，节奏和成本都更合理。 在 AutoClaw 里直接调用这两款模型 两个模型不需要分开安装、分开开通：它们都已内置在 AutoClaw 里，新建任务时直接选择即可，上下文、工作文件和交付物都在同一个工作区，切模型不打断工作。新模型上线即接入也是常态——GLM-5.3-Flash 发布当天就在 AutoClaw 可用，不存在等适配的窗口期。 具体到日常使用，常规任务默认直接下单，AutoClaw 会按任务特点匹配合适的模型；明确的复杂工程、长程研究、大型代码库任务，指定 GLM-5.3；高频轻量、多轮迭代的任务，指定 GLM-5.3-Flash。切换过程中已生成的工作文件和交付物不受影响——你可以在同一个项目里先用 GLM-5.3 打底，再切 GLM-5.3-Flash 做轻量迭代，反之亦然。项目做到一半换模型同样成立：文件、对话和已交付的产物都在，随时切。 任务光谱：常见工作的对号入座 把日常任务摊开，大部分都能在这张表里找到位置： 任务 推荐模型 理由 起草/修改邮件、文案、通知 GLM-5.3-Flash 单轮或少数几轮，快和迭代体验优先 截图、图表、扫描件转结构化数据 GLM-5.3-Flash 原生多模态主场 长文档摘要与要点整理 GLM-5.3-Flash 混合架构下长上下文开销低 多份表格合并、清洗、核对 GLM-5.3-Flash 规则明确的高频数据处理 月度/季度总结的素材聚合 GLM-5.3-Flash 量大、步骤多但单步轻 竞品研究报告（搜集到成稿） GLM-5.3 多工具搜集、交叉验证、长程成稿 端到端开发（需求→实现→测试） GLM-5.3 复杂工程与 Agentic Coding 深度调试与代码重构 GLM-5.3 大型代码库里的持续定位 长程研究任务（边查边验证） GLM-5.3 需要持续理解目标与多步骤依赖 一份长报告的框架与论证 GLM-5.3 结构与论证质量决定报告上限 同一份报告的第三轮修订 GLM-5.3-Flash 轻量迭代，反馈要快 定时批量任务（每日汇总、盯页面） GLM-5.3-Flash 高频连续执行，成本敏感 规律很清楚：看两件事——单次任务的工作量和整个流程的步数。工作量大、步骤之间有依赖的，往上选；量大但每步都轻的，往下选。 组合用法：一个项目里怎么让两个模型接力 真正提效的用法不是二选一，而是让两个模型在同一项目里接力。以一份竞品研究报告为例，官网公开能力支持这样的分工：GLM-5.3 负责需要持续理解目标的部分——拆解研究问题、多工具搜集与交叉验证、搭建报告骨架和关键论证；GLM-5.3-Flash 负责高频轻量环节——图表和资料的快速整理、逐轮的措辞修订、格式与排版迭代。重活在旗舰上做深，轻改在 Flash 上跑快，整份报告的节奏会比全程用一个模型更顺。 接力不需要复杂操作：在 AutoClaw 里按任务阶段切换模型即可，上下文和已交付的文件都在同一个工作区里。一个常见的节奏是把项目分成三段：开题和研究阶段用 GLM-5.3，把问题定义、资料基础和框架立住；制作阶段视内容重量灵活选择，重的论证继续用 GLM-5.3，轻的整理交给 GLM-5.3-Flash；修订和交付阶段几乎全程 GLM-5.3-Flash，因为这一阶段要的是快和多轮。 两种典型工作节奏，模型组合完全不同 看看两种真实的工作状态，模型搭配思路截然不同。一种是一天处理二十件小事的节奏：早上整理三份会议记录、上午归档一批截图资料、中午出两版文案、下午核对五张表——每件事都是单轮或少数几轮的轻任务，这种日子几乎全程 GLM-5.3-Flash，要的就是每件事都快、当天全清。另一种是一周跟一个长项目的节奏：周一立框架、周三中期检查、周五看阶段产出，任务始终悬着、依赖不断累积——这种日子 GLM-5.3 是主力，中途的边角活才切 Flash。 大多数人两种节奏都有。所以模型不是选一次定终身，而是跟着当天的工作构成走：小事扎堆的日子放开用 Flash，攻坚的日子把 5.3 派上去。 怎么发现你用错了模型 用错模型是有信号的。如果你发现自己在反复把背景贴回对话里，任务做着做着模型就忘了目标，需要你不断重申——这是长程任务用了轻量模型，该换 GLM-5.3。反过来，改几行文案也要等很久，是日常高频任务上了旗舰，换 GLM-5.3-Flash 立刻见效。多步骤任务中途丢依赖（第二步做完忘了第一步的约定），同样说明该用旗舰；而截图、图表这类视觉内容处理不动，则要想到 GLM-5.3-Flash 的原生多模态才是主场。长程任务跑着跑着质量下降，说明验证和收尾阶段应该留给 GLM-5.3 收官。 另外，AutoClaw 也支持切换 DeepSeek 系列模型；本文聚焦 GLM 两款模型的分工，系列内其它模型的定位见官网模型页。 GLM 家族的完整分工 把视野放大到整个 GLM 家族，官网模型页给出了清晰的分层：GLM-5.3 是复杂工程与长程任务的旗舰；GLM-5.3-Flash 用原生多模态和混合架构覆盖高频轻量场景；GLM-5.2 面向项目级上下文和长程交付，适合需要反复分析、修改和验证、要持续保持上下文的项目；GLM-5-Turbo 为连续运行的 Agent 工作流优化，接流程明确但步骤较多的标准化任务；GLM-5V-Turbo 主打视觉理解与视觉编程，看懂截图、界面和视频再转化为行动。五款模型在 AutoClaw 里都可切换，按任务特点各就各位即可。 常见误区 Flash 是"低配"，重要任务不敢用。 官网口径是它在多项基准与实际任务中超越 GLM-5.2——上一代旗舰级模型的能力水平，处理日常办公与轻量开发绰绰有余。选型看的是任务匹配，不是型号大小。

blogs.description: 三种桌面 AI Agent 路线六维度对比：安装、数据边界、执行、模型归属、成本、适合谁，附三个真实任务跑法与 30 秒决策表。
blogs.content: 返回博客 AutoClaw、Manus 和自部署开源 Agent 有什么区别？三种路线怎么选 产品 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月6日 三种桌面 AI Agent 路线六维度对比：安装、数据边界、执行、模型归属、成本、适合谁，附三个真实任务跑法与 30 秒决策表。 AutoClaw、Manus 和自部署开源 Agent 有什么区别？三种路线怎么选 选桌面 AI Agent，本质上是在三种工作方式里选：装一个现成的（AutoClaw），在云端用（Manus），或者自己把开源的 Agent 框架跑起来（自部署）。没有哪条路线绝对更好，取决于你处理什么数据、做什么工作、愿意承担多少维护。本文把三条路线放进六个维度里对比，其中包括一个常被忽略的维度：底下的模型是谁做的。后文有 30 秒决策表。 我们怎么比的 下文每个维度都用同样的三个输入：各产品官方文档（截至 2026 年 11 月）、AutoClaw 自家工作流的使用经验，以及另外两条路线的公开资料。价格、集成、模型可用性这类经常变化的内容，请以各产品官网当前说明为准。 三条路线 AutoClaw（一键本地安装）。 智谱出品的桌面 AI Agent，一键安装在 Windows、macOS 上，直接操作你电脑里的文件、浏览器和工具。文件和操作留在本机，只有完成任务所需的内容会发送给模型。50+ 内置技能开箱即用；目标模式（设定目标，规划-执行-验证-迭代）、Agent 集群模式（并行多角色执行加复核）、定时任务、多 Agent 记忆隔离都有；飞书、企业微信、微信等 IM 可以直接接入使用。 Manus（云端原生）。 商业云端 Agent 平台。任务在 Manus 的云端环境执行：你在网页或应用里给出目标，它在云端分解、执行并交付。优势是无需安装、多设备体验一致、集成生态丰富（浏览器扩展、移动端等）。对应的取舍是任务跑在云端，文件需要上传，按套餐和用量付费。 自部署开源方案（以 OpenClaw 框架为代表）。 开源 Agent 框架社区活跃，自部署意味着最大的控制力和可定制性，也意味着最大的责任：环境搭建、API 密钥管理、安全加固、版本维护都由你负责。 选型前，先问自己六个问题 这六个问题的答案，基本决定了你该走哪条路线： 你处理的文件里有没有合同、财务、客户资料这类敏感内容？ 你的任务是每次都不一样，还是长期重复？ 团队里有没有人能管部署和运维？ 协作主要发生在哪个平台：飞书、企业微信还是浏览器？ 预算是固定订阅更好预测，还是可以接受随用量浮动？ 未来半年任务量是稳定、增长还是不确定？ 带着这六个答案往下读，每个维度的结论会自然对号入座。 维度一：安装与上手 AutoClaw Manus 自部署开源 安装 原生安装包，约 1 分钟 无需安装，浏览器/应用即用 数小时到数天（环境+配置+调试） 技术门槛 无 无 高（命令行、API、运维） 持续维护 官方自动更新 平台托管 版本与安全补丁自己负责 结论： 只想尽快开始干活，AutoClaw 和 Manus 都合适；自部署第一天的成本就高出一个量级。三种路线的"开始"成本结构不同：本地安装是装完即用，云端是打开即用，自部署是装完还要调。 维度二：数据边界 AutoClaw Manus 自部署开源 文件存储 文件留在本机，仅将任务所需内容发送给模型 上传到云端执行 自己掌控（取决于你的配置） 安全责任 官方更新维护，数据主要在本机处理 在平台方 完全在你 适合的数据 本地文件、日常办公与专业材料 一般办公材料 有安全团队的企业 三条路线最深的分界线在这里：文件放在哪里处理，谁来为它负责。AutoClaw 的文件和操作在你自己的电脑上，只有完成任务所需的内容会发送给模型；云端平台的文件需要上传到平台；自部署则完全取决于你自己的配置和纪律。 如果你每天处理合同、财务数据或客户文件，建议先看这一维度。需要注意：无论哪种路线，只要用到云端模型，相关内容就会发送给模型服务方。涉及保密协议的材料，请先确认协议是否允许使用 AI 服务，再决定怎么用。 维度三：执行位置决定能做什么 AutoClaw Manus 自部署开源 执行位置 本地，直接操作你的文件和浏览器 云端环境 你的基础设施 深度任务 目标模式自主循环 + 集群模式多角色复核 blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: 无需写代码的网页采集五步法：字段清单、试抓样本、批量采集、清洗对账，附可复制任务描述，可用 AutoClaw 完成。
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 网页抓取怎么做？无需写代码的信息采集流程 教程 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月3日 无需写代码的网页采集五步法：字段清单、试抓样本、批量采集、清洗对账，附可复制任务描述，可用 AutoClaw 完成。 AI 网页抓取怎么做？无需写代码的信息采集流程 网页抓取的难点从来不是"能不能拿到数据"，而是"拿到的数据能不能用"。列表页要翻页，内容页字段对不上，页面一改版采集就断，价格和日期混在文本里没法统计。AI 改变的不是抓取本身，而是分工：你描述要什么字段、从哪些页面拿，由 AI 去读页面结构、执行采集、清洗口径、留下核对记录——不需要你写选择器脚本。 先想清楚三件事，再决定怎么抓 动手前先回答：要什么字段、从哪些页面拿、拿多久一次。这三件事决定了采集方式，也决定了哪些环节要人工处理。 页面情况 适合的方式 注意点 公开列表页 + 详情页 直接采集，按字段清单输出 记录每条数据的来源 URL 需要登录才能看 用账号使用者的登录态执行 账号、验证码由人处理，不代做 动态渲染（滚动加载） 让 AI 沿页面滚动逐屏读取 确认最后一屏的判断依据 数据以 PDF / 附件存在 先取附件，再做表格提取 表格提取复核见配套教程 有一类页面不建议碰：明确禁止采集、涉及个人隐私或需要绕过权限的内容。抓取用于公开信息的整理，边界要自己守住。 第一步：把"我要什么"写成字段清单 不要上来就说"把这个网站的数据抓下来"。字段清单至少包含：每条记录要哪些字段（名称、价格、日期、链接……）、什么算一条记录（一个商品？一条公告？一家公司？）、以哪个页面为准（列表页还是详情页）。这份清单就是后面核对的对账基准。 第二步：让 AI 先读结构，试抓几条 把两三个示例链接和字段清单交给 AI，让它先说明页面结构（列表在哪、翻页规律、目标字段在页面什么位置），抓出几条样本。先看样本再批量，是避免"抓了三千行、全抓错了列"的唯一办法。 第三步：批量采集，记录来源 批量执行时，每条数据都应带上来源 URL 和采集时间。这不是形式主义：价格、库存、政策随时会变，没有来源的采集结果，过一周就无法判断哪些需要重查。 第四步：清洗口径，别把文本当数字 抓回来的"1,299 元""约 3.4 万""2026年10月"是文本，不是数字。金额去掉货币符号存数值，日期统一格式，"约""以上"这类模糊表述单独保留在备注列。所有清洗规则要留下记录——哪些值改了、按什么规则改的。 第五步：对账，再使用 交付前核对：记录总数与列表页分页数能否对上；抽查若干条回原页面对照；金额、日期列能否排序求和不出错。对不上先查原因，不要为了让数字好看而调整数据。 用 AutoClaw 做网页采集 AutoClaw 是智谱推出的通用 AI Agent，能跨浏览器和文件持续工作。把字段清单和示例链接交给它，它会打开页面、识别结构、执行采集并输出 Excel；采集完成后继续让它们做清洗、汇总和核对表。抓取解决"这次拿全"，如果要盯着同一个页面长期变化，那是另一个任务形态——定时监控与提醒，做法见《网页变化监控怎么设置》。 可直接复制的任务描述： 请采集以下页面列表中的数据。字段要求：（逐项列出）。先读取页面结构并给出 3 条样本让我确认字段对应关系；确认后批量采集，每条记录附带来源 URL 和采集时间；翻页采集直到最后一页，说明你判断"最后一页"的依据。输出 Excel 明细表和采集记录说明；无法读取或字段缺失的页面单独列出，不要编造补齐。 交付前核对清单 每条记录都有来源 URL 和采集时间 记录总数与页面分页数能对上 抽查的样本与原页面一致 金额、日期是可计算的格式，不是文本 字段缺失或读取失败的页面已单独列出 清洗规则有记录，没有"静默修改" 常见问题 完全不会代码也能用吗？ 可以。描述字段和页面，由 AI 完成读取与采集；你要把关的是字段清单和对账结果。 会不会把网站抓坏或账号被封？ 只采集公开页面、控制频率、遵守站点条款；需要登录的页面用你自己的账号，权限与验证码由人处理。批量任务先小规模试抓。 和网页变化监控是一回事吗？ 不是。抓取是"一次把数据拿全"，监控是"盯着页面等它变化"。先采集建底表，再用监控盯增量，两个任务配合使用。 结论 网页采集的可靠程度，取决于字段清单是否清楚、样本是否先确认、结果是否对过账。把这三件事做扎实，AI 负责读页面和执行，你负责定义和核对，不需要一行代码也能拿到能用的数据。 下载 AutoClaw，让 AI 分身进入你的对话框： https://autoclaw.zhipuai.cn/
